comment: Known compliance deviations accepted by policy. Accept a deviation only when exact compatibility is infeasible and the observable impact is immaterial. Entries must match exactly; tolerances must be query-specific and bounded. Any drift (different query, different diff shape, over-margin values, or unused allowlist entry) fails reconciliation so regressions surface.

tolerances.reason: ClickHouse native modulo uses x - trunc(x / y) * y instead of Go/Prometheus math.Mod, which causes tiny float drift on large operands. Accept only when the rerun against both APIs stays within a 1e-6 absolute margin and labels/timestamps still match exactly.

entries.reason: Prometheus topk's tie-break is a storage-layer implementation detail. promql/engine.go:1052 calls querier.Select with sortSeries=false, so the TSDB SeriesSet is iterated in its native postings order (essentially series-ref / scrape-discovery order). aggregationK (engine.go:3776) then iterates 'for si := range inputMatrix' preserving that order, and the heap replacement at engine.go:3865 uses a strict '<' comparison (group.heap[0].F < s.F), so on an exact tie the new element does NOT displace the heap root — first-seen wins. That first-seen order is not derivable from labels alone (labels.Hash / labels.StableHash give alphabetical order; the fixture's TSDB order differs). Reproducing Prom's tie-break exactly would require mirroring its storage layer. On this fixture, demo_memory_usage_bytes series across instance demo.promlabs.com:10000/10001/10002 occasionally hit the same float value (173015040) at the same timestep; Prom and the shim disagree on which instance survives the cut. Affects only exact-value ties, which are rare in real data. Verified against prometheus@57821524d. See harness/compliance/README.md section 'topk tie-break ordering'.
